title: JT-60SA Completes Major Upgrades — Integrated Commissioning Begins for Restart
detail: On May 15, 2026, ANS Nuclear Newswire and Fusion for Energy announced that JT-60SA — the world's largest operational superconducting tokamak — has completed a comprehensive post-first-plasma upgrade programme and is ready to resume experiments, with integrated commissioning underway. Located at the National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology (QST) in Naka, Japan, JT-60SA is a joint Europe–Japan project under the Broader Approach agreement. Upgrades include: a new carbon-based first wall and divertor replacing components damaged during the initial 2023 campaign; 8-meter in-vessel coils wound directly inside the machine to enable high-speed plasma position control (critical for disruption avoidance); additional NBI and ECRH heating systems boosting total input power capacity; new European cryopumps; and advanced diagnostic systems. Jerónimo García took over as project leader on May 14, 2026. Plasma heating experiments are planned for late 2026, with over 150 scientific proposals under review from teams across 24 EU member states and Japan. JT-60SA is designed to sustain high-performance plasmas for up to 100 seconds and serves as a critical experimental platform for informing ITER operations and future DEMO reactor design.

title: China's 15th Five-Year Plan Names Fusion Among Eight National 'Frontier Technology' Priorities
detail: China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) formally designates fusion energy as one of eight national 'frontier technology' priorities, alongside artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and advanced materials. The plan is backed by over $6.5 billion in government fusion investment since 2023. New fusion facilities — including the BEST tokamak — are under construction as part of China's accelerating programme. The designation builds on China's record-setting plasma research: EAST achieved 1,066 seconds at over 100 million°C in January 2025, and the China Fusion Engineering Test Reactor (CFETR) is in engineering development targeting a 2 GW test reactor by approximately 2035. The 15th FYP prioritisation signals that China intends to sustain and grow fusion investment at a pace matching or exceeding Western government programmes combined, making the fusion energy race increasingly multipolar.
